29 Which statement gives a condition that enables diffraction to occur?
A
A source of waves moves towards a stationary observer.
B
A wave is partially blocked by an obstacle.
C
Two coherent waves are superposed.
D
Two waves of equal speed and frequency are travelling through the same part of a medium
in opposite directions.

hints: Look at what each statement describes: movement of a source in A, blocking by an obstacle in B, adding waves in C and D.
Recall that diffraction is the spreading of a single wave when part of its wavefront is stopped by a gap or edge of size similar to its wavelength.
Compare the other statements to interference and stationary waves: C needs coherence for interference and D with opposite directions forms a stationary wave.
walkthrough: Identify the process to test: diffraction is the spreading of waves past an edge or through a gap into the geometrical shadow.
State the physical requirement: part of the wave must be blocked so the remaining unblocked part acts as a new source of wavelets that spread out.
Check statement A: a source moving towards an observer changes the observed frequency. This is the Doppler effect, not blocking and spreading.

Check statements C and D: two coherent waves superposed give interference, and two identical waves in opposite directions give a stationary wave. Both need two waves, not one wave meeting an obstacle.
Check statement B: a wave partially blocked by an obstacle has its wavefront truncated and then spreads beyond the edge. This matches the condition for diffraction. This is option B.

A.explanation: A moving source and stationary observer changes observed wavelength and frequency, which is the Doppler effect, not diffraction.

B.explanation: When a wavefront is cut by an edge, slit or obstacle it spreads into the shadow region, which is diffraction.

C.explanation: Superposition of two coherent waves with constant phase difference produces interference, not diffraction on its own.

D.explanation: Two identical waves travelling in opposite directions superpose to form a stationary wave with nodes and antinodes, not diffraction.
